newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Euro assembly says Tapie not forced to go to jail.
newsitem.headline: Euro assembly says Tapie not forced to go to jail.

text.p: Bernard Tapie, the bankrupt former tycoon, French politician and soccer boss, is not obliged to go to jail until his mandate as a Euro-deputy expires on February 17, the European Parliament said on Monday.
The news was unlikely to prevent Tapie spending his first night in jail on Monday, the first of many if the French Supreme Court rejects his appeal on Tuesday.

The parliament's Rules Committee said in a letter to the assembly's president Jose-Maria Gil-Robles Gil-Delgado that Tapie would benefit from immunity until the assembly declared his seat vacant on February 17.
"The date this vacancy arises should coincide with the date the European Parliament takes note of it," the letter said.

By law Tapie, who has expressed terror at the prospect of going to jail, must report to prison on the eve of the hearing on his appeal against an eight-month sentence for rigging a soccer match. Otherwise his case would be scrapped.
But he still had a few possible legal emergency exits and television crews mounting guard outside Paris's La Sante prison were kept guessing all day whether he would actually come.
The Supreme Court will rule on Tuesday on Tapie's final appeal against the sentence for bribing players to fix a soccer match between Marseille and Valenciennes in 1993.

Justice sources doubted that the Supreme Court would put off Tuesday's ruling because of lingering doubts about whether he was still protected from imprisonment by his membership of the European Parliament, his last political mandate.
A French court last year ruled he was ineligible for public office because he was personally bankrupt.
